clue.text: Red backs? Lilo tip for swimming pool

definitions.note: pool is a cue game played on a table with pockets

indicators.note: letters that are swimming are moving about freely, so the fodder words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An Australian redback spider lurking on an inflatable lilo: advice for anyone at the swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red backs' and 'swimming pool' both suggest Australian spiders and bathing, but 'swimming' is the anagram signal and 'pool' is the game. A Lilo is a British brand of inflatable airbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Pool is the American name for the cue game, a form of billiards played on a table with six pockets.

clue.text: They bow as terrorist group gets time in prison

indicators.note: in says the group and time sit within the prison word

parts.note: prison cells
IS is short for Islamic State

explanation.surface: A news report: a terror gang member is jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrorist group' tempts CELL, but here it is IS (Islamic State); the prison is CELLS.
explanation.definitionFit: String players draw a bow across their instruments, so they are people who bow.

clue.text: Meeting Charlie in one boozer

parts.note: one as the article a

indicators.note: in places Charlie's letter within the drunkard word

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Bumping into a pal called Charlie inside a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boozer' is British slang for a pub, but here it is the drinker. Ascot is a famous English racecourse whose race days are called meetings.
explanation.definitionFit: A race meeting is a day of horse racing, and Royal Ascot is the best-known one.

clue.text: Smalls remain outside for idle …

parts.note: to linger is to stay on, to remain

indicators.note: the outside of the word idle means its two end letters only

explanation.surface: Underwear left out to lie around idle, leading into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smalls' is British slang for underwear. The ellipsis links into 5 Down, whose surface continues the thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Smalls is a British word for underclothes, and women's underwear is sold as this.

clue.text: … mark in smalls remains

indicators.note: in puts the mark inside the pair of letters for smalls

parts.note: small is S, so two smalls are S and S
a tick is a check mark

explanation.surface: A stain on underwear that won't come out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smalls' again suggests underwear, as in 4 Down, but here it is S twice.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick is to stay put, so something that sticks stays where it is.

clue.text: Patient one cross in place for work

parts.note: Job, the Biblical figure famed for his patience
in football, to centre the ball is to cross it into the middle

explanation.surface: A long-suffering person grows cross while waiting at the benefits office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' reads as angry; it is the football pass. A Jobcentre is a UK government office helping people find work.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the British public office where the unemployed look for jobs, so a place for finding work.

clue.text: Improved attention span for top-grade student

indicators.note: to span is to stretch across, so the attention word goes around the grade and student

parts.note: to pay heed is to pay attention
A is the top grade in a marking scheme
L is a learner driver, a student

explanation.surface: A star pupil's ability to concentrate got better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attention span' looks like one phrase, but 'span' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something healed has got better or been made well, a synonym for improved in health.

clue.text: Power arm? A special gym to work out for sporting event?

parts.note: P is the symbol for power

indicators.note: working out the letters means exercising them into a new order

explanation.surface: A strong arm built up with a special gym workout for an athletics competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to work out' suits a gym but is the anagram signal. The question mark hints that a Power arm belongs at an event for disabled athletes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Paralympics are the major international multi-sport competition for athletes with disabilities.

clue.text: One maybe put on runs: deliveries knocked over the top

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries

indicators.note: these letters are placed over the top of the runs, enclosing them

parts.note: to hit is to knock
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A batsman scoring runs, smashing bowling over the top for six.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is cricket: an over is six balls bowled. 'over the top' also hints at a lofted shot, but it signals the enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a garment, and garments are things a person puts on to wear.

clue.text: Great first love letter

indicators.note: first places the love letter at the front, before the word for great

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O
mega is slang for great

explanation.surface: A wonderful first love letter, the romantic kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love letter' looks like a phrase; love is O and letter is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the last letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Breakfast supplier back to cook scrambled egg roll right away

indicators.note: the back of the word cook is its final letter
scrambled letters are mixed up, like scrambled egg
right taken away means the letter R is removed

parts.note: R stands for right

explanation.surface: A kitchen instruction: scramble the egg and roll it immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrambled egg' looks like food; 'scrambled' is the anagram signal working on EGG plus OLL.
explanation.definitionFit: The cereal firm is a famous maker of breakfast cornflakes.

clue.text: Part of organ not quite audible around old church

indicators.note: around says the trimmed word wraps the old and church letters
not quite means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: clear, as in clearly heard
the last letter dropped

explanation.surface: A church organ whose sound barely carries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests the church instrument; it is the ear. 'not quite' drops the last letter of CLEAR to give CLEA.
explanation.definitionFit: The spiral cavity of the inner ear, and the ear is a sense organ.

clue.text: Model to pose for job

parts.note: the Model T Ford
to pose a question is to ask

explanation.surface: A model being asked to pose for a photo shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: The Model T was an early Ford car, so Model gives T.
explanation.definitionFit: A task is a piece of work to be done, as a job is.

clue.text: Now feel bad about director cutting salary

indicators.note: cutting into the salary word means sitting inside it

parts.note: pay is salary
to resent is to feel bitter about

explanation.surface: An employee resents the boss slashing wages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'director cutting salary' reads like a pay cut, but 'cutting' signals insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe the current time, contemporary rather than past or future.

clue.text: Wearing eye make-up, Britney Spears primarily concealing bags

indicators.note: concealing means the initials hide the other letters between them
primarily picks the first letters of the two names

parts.note: in, as dressed in
eyeliner, shortened to liner

explanation.surface: The pop star in heavy eyeliner, hiding her face under handbags.
explanation.walkthrough: Bin liners are plastic bags lining rubbish bins.
explanation.definitionFit: These are plastic sacks that line a rubbish bin, so they are a kind of bag.

clue.text: Fire single sniper shot

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or broken, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lone sniper firing one round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' and 'shot' both suggest guns; 'Fire' means to stir someone's imagination.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire someone up is to rouse their enthusiasm, a synonym for stirring them.

clue.text: Mismanage second team that's winning

parts.note: a crew is a team
up means ahead, as in one goal up

explanation.surface: A sports manager bungling the reserve side while it leads.
explanation.definitionFit: To screw something up is slang for botching it or handling it badly.

clue.text: Help to protect Britain; politician that might cause upset

indicators.note: protecting means the help signal wraps round Britain

parts.note: SOS is the distress call
a Tory is a UK Conservative

explanation.surface: A call to defend the nation from a Conservative who might stir up trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' suggests turmoil, but means sadness; a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A tearjerking tale told to win sympathy is meant to make listeners sad and emotional.

clue.text: Were covers not stained ultimately in the morning with this?

definitions.text: Were covers not stained ultimately in the morning with this?

indicators.note: covers says the first word wraps around the letters picked out
ultimately takes the last letter of each of the two words

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem

explanation.surface: Bedsheets checked in the morning for stains after a night's dream.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is an extended definition: the question hints at the reason sheets might be stained by morning.
explanation.definitionFit: A nocturnal emission during sleep, which would leave bedding stained by daybreak.

clue.text: 27 on pub game

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the cross-reference goes on the end of the pub word

parts.note: your local is your regular pub
27 Across is a classic, and the Derby at Epsom is one of the English Classic races

explanation.surface: A cross-reference followed by a pub game.
explanation.walkthrough: A local derby is a match between two teams from the same town.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a sports fixture between neighbouring rivals, a kind of game or match.

clue.text: Groom mostly attractive and sweet

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: to comb hair is to groom it
the final letter dropped
fit is British slang for attractive

explanation.surface: A bridegroom who is mostly handsome and kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groom' and 'sweet' suggest a wedding; a comfit is a sugar-coated sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A comfit is a confection: a seed or nut coated in sugar.

clue.text: Crude painting? What gallery finally frames?

indicators.note: frames says the query word goes around the painting

parts.note: eh? is a way of asking what?
art

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of gallery

explanation.surface: A rough painting raises the question of what a gallery would frame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frames' looks like the gallery's job, but it means the EH holds ART.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthy humour is coarse and vulgar, a synonym for crude.

clue.text: Relating to listener in two ticks

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words two ticks

explanation.surface: A speaker's two-second aside to an audience member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'listener' means the ear, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Otic means of or relating to the ear, and the ear is the body's listener.

clue.text: Foreign film

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means strange or from elsewhere, and is also the title of a famous science-fiction horror film.

clue.text: One gave charity millions, one recluse admits

parts.note: one as the article a

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the recluse word holds the millions letter

parts.note: a loner keeps away from others

explanation.surface: A hermit who quietly gave away millions.
explanation.walkthrough: An almoner was historically an official who handed out alms to the poor.
explanation.definitionFit: An almoner was a person who distributed alms, money given in charity.

clue.text: Winged sandals in Australia? American's going out

indicators.note: out means out of order, so the remaining letters are rearranged
going means leaving, so those letters are taken from the country

parts.note: US, the United States, is the American country

explanation.surface: Footwear spotted Down Under while an American tourist leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going' removes US from AUSTRALIA, leaving ATRALIA, and 'out' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the winged shoes worn by the Greek messenger god Hermes, Mercury to the Romans.

clue.text: Rider thrown off maiden

definitions.note: a maiden is a dialect word for a clothes-horse for drying laundry

indicators.note: thrown off suggests the letters fall in disorder, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A jockey unseated by a maiden horse, one that has never won.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maiden' looks like racing (a horse yet to win) but is a clothes-horse, a frame for drying washing.
explanation.definitionFit: Maiden is an old regional name for a clothes-horse, a frame on which laundry is hung to dry.

clue.text: Play score and hear a classic, perhaps

indicators.note: play means move about loosely, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Put on some music and listen to a classic piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'classic' suggests music; the Classics are five major English flat races, such as the Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: The English Classics are five top flat races, so a Classic is an example of one.
